evidence: deepseek: "Check JOB condition" followed by separate "Check LOAD 1"; gpt-oss: "if p1 + p2 > T" then "if sum1 > T"; qwen: "Check each job for JOB certificate" followed by "Check each component for LOAD certificate"
affordance_in_statement: For every provided test case, exactly one of the following isolated subsystems is inherently impossible to assign; ... even if we completely ignore Exclusivity and all other items; ... even if we completely ignore Causality and the other component.
removal_suggestion: Do not explicitly expose JOB and LOAD as independently checkable subsystems with clauses saying the other constraints may be ignored. Present the certificates through an indirect placement-audit scenario, requiring the solver to identify which constraints and objects participate in the failed audit while preserving the same underlying feasibility meaning.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Checks each item's two lengths against T, then checks the component-wise sums against T.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The JOB and LOAD certificates explicitly allow all unrelated items and constraints to be ignored.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses p1 + p2 > T for JOB and sum1/sum2 > T for LOAD, with a fixed priority order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement separates per-item causality from per-component exclusivity into isolated subsystems.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Separately tests every job and each component's aggregate interval capacity.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The explicit JOB/LOAD bullet definitions make the feasibility checks independent.

common_affordance: The statement explicitly decomposes the answer into an independently tested per-item JOB condition or per-component LOAD condition.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It checks only whether an individual p1 or p2 exceeds T for LOAD, instead of detecting that multiple individually fitting intervals can collectively exceed T.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit isolated-subsystem bullets and their 'even if we completely ignore' clauses with an indirect scenario describing two possible failed placement audits, without naming the independent per-item and per-component feasibility tests directly.
